label: build-55
system: You are a pragmatic solo developer who has shipped consumer apps and been burned by inference bills. You cost things honestly and you have no stake in whether this idea is good. Output JSON only.
user:
Cost this consumer app idea as a real build.

IDEA
{
  "id": 55,
  "title": "Lookback Ledger",
  "unlock": "Frontier reading dropped to ten cents a million input tokens with a million-token window and cached input at roughly a 90% discount, so an agent can read five years of a parent's bank statements, bills and receipts, categorise every line and keep the running record current for pennies a month - the work a paid bookkeeper billed by the hour.",
  "pain": "Adult children paying an aging parent's bills, categorising the costs and settling up with siblings keep it all in a spiral binder because no consumer tool produces documentation that survives a Medicaid lookback.",
  "audience": "Adult children in the US who share paying an aging parent's bills with one or more siblings",
  "mechanic": "shared_ledger",
  "wedge": "One job only: photograph or forward a bill paid on the parent's behalf, the agent reads it, assigns the category and the payer, and writes one line to a shared family record with the image attached - starting from the month the first sibling signs up, not from a full historical import.",
  "moat": "switching_cost_of_history",
  "model": "subscription",
  "loop": "invite_for_function",
  "kill": [
    "Fewer than 40% of paying households add a second sibling to the ledger within 30 days, which means it is a single-person spreadsheet and not a shared record.",
    "Line-level categorisation of photographed bills and receipts agrees with the family's own labelling on under 95% of a 1,000-document audit, so someone still has to check every line by hand.",
    "Median months of continuous use falls below 9, meaning the record never gets long enough to be worth keeping.",
    "Blended model cost exceeds $0.30 per active household per month once photo volume settles at roughly 30 documents a month."
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "Not absorbable: it never touches calendar, email or contacts, it is a financial audit record whose value is the five-year run of evidence it accumulates, so a general assistant that answers one question well still cannot hand a family the documented history; and the obvious first suggestion for this audience is a care-coordination or medication app, because nobody thinks of bookkeeping as the thing that is actually eating their evenings.",
  "why_now": "End to end: the specific hourly task was a bookkeeper reading a stack of statements and receipts, sorting them into categories and reconciling who paid what, and at $0.10 per million input tokens with a million-token window [3][5] an agent does the whole read-sort-reconcile pass with no person behind it - the family only taps to confirm a line it flags as unclear, which is a confirmation, not a wage."
}

2026 facts you must use:
- Frontier text inference is about $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.40 out.
- Apple's on-device and Private Cloud Compute models cost $0 in cloud API fees
  for Small Business Program members under 2M lifetime downloads.
- Real-time voice runs $0.005 to $0.018 per minute on cheap stacks and up to
  $0.091 on flagship speech-to-speech. Model choice is the business model.
- Median consumer subscription price is about $10 monthly, $35 yearly.
- Typical paid conversion for a freemium consumer app is 2-4%.

Return JSON:
{
  "stack": "concrete: platform, language, model choice, backend, store",
  "milestones": ["3-6 items, each a shippable week or two of work"],
  "build_cost_usd": <number: real cost to a solo builder using AI assistance>,
  "weeks_to_v1": <number>,
  "inference_cost_user_month": <number: blended cost per ACTIVE user, not per payer>,
  "price_month": <number>,
  "expected_conversion": <number 0-1>,
  "riskiest_technical_assumption": "one sentence",
  "cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption": "one sentence"
}

Be honest. If this needs continuous voice or video generation, say what that
actually costs per active user. An idea that cannot clear its own inference bill
should show that in the numbers, not be flattered.
